I try several alternative widths to see if they reproduce the labeled areas of 13.4 and 6.9, but nothing lines up cleanly. Then I notice that simply summing the labeled horizontal dimensions (0.30+5.86+0.115+4.00+0.30) gives 10.575, which doesn't match the stated overall width of 10.00 — meaning the dimension chain itself is internally inconsistent, independent of the actual geometry, which is a standalone error worth flagging.

That width doesn't match the total interior width either, so the area labels aren't internally consistent with each other. I'm wondering if the discrepancy stems from a single wall being shifted in the original geometry, which would explain why multiple derived areas appear stale relative to the drawing — so I want to test whether moving the interior wall position resolves the inconsistencies.

I try matching digit patterns: 31.2 could be a truncated 37.12, 13.4 a truncated 14.24, 6.9 a truncated 7.67. I also test whether a uniform scale factor explains the discrepancy — 37.12×0.84≈31.2 works for WOHNEN but fails for SCHLAFEN (14.237×0.84≈11.96, not 13.4), so that hypothesis doesn't hold either.

I also try shifting SCHLAFEN's boundary to the wall centerline instead of the face, but that makes the area worse, not better. At this point I'm fairly confident the dimension chain itself doesn't sum correctly — 30+5.86+11 doesn't add up to the stated total, which seems like the real source of the discrepancy.

Checking the coordinates more carefully, the wall gap and the door arc don't actually overlap — the arc's flat edge sits right at the top of the white break rather than spanning it, confirming the door symbol is misaligned with the wall opening. I also verify the vertical wall segment runs continuously without any gap, which helps pin down exactly where the real opening is.

Checking the entrance and BAD doors for reference confirms they look fine. The entrance door hinge sits at the inner wall face with the leaf sweeping outward past the outer wall line, which seems like a plausible CAD convention rather than an error.

Verifying the closed-leaf and open-position lines for the entrance door, they match the opening span correctly, and the BAD door's hinge and leaf also align with its opening. So it seems only the SCHLAFEN door is mirrored incorrectly.

Checking the title block and scale notation, everything lines up — plan number, date, and the 7.00 vertical dimension all check out. I notice SCHLAFEN and BAD lack height dimensions, but that's more of a completeness gap than an actual error, so I won't flag it strongly. The cm/metre unit conventions also look standard.

Verifying the overall dimension lines: the 10.00 span matches the full outer width, and the 7.00 vertical dimension checks out at 198.42 between its endpoints. Tallying everything I've confirmed — chain labels, overall dimensions, areas, doors, scale, wall thicknesses — I'm satisfied I've covered all the text and vector data without missing any annotations, so I'm ready to finalize.
